entities.summary:
Monsignor François Ducaud-Bourget (1934-1984) was a prominent traditionalist Roman Catholic French prelate, priest and close ally of Archbishop Marcel Lefebvre.

As the Archbishop of Toulouse, Ducaud-Bourget played a pivotal role in the French resistance against the secularization of the Catholic Church, utilizing his clerical authority to counter the influence of the French government. He also spearheaded the creation of the Society of St. Pius X, which aimed to preserve Catholic traditions and practices in the face of modernism and secularism.

Ducaud-Bourget's actions had far-reaching consequences, influencing the trajectory of Catholicism in France and beyond. His leadership helped shape the modern Catholic movement, which continues to impact the Church's teachings and practices today.

In the words of Archbishop Lefebvre, 'Monsignor Ducaud-Bourget was a priest, a priest of God, a priest of the Holy Father, a priest of the Church, and a priest of the people. He was a priest who was not afraid to take a stand for what he believed in, even when it meant going against the will of the world.'

This quote encapsulates the essence of Ducaud-Bourget's legacy, one that continues to inspire and challenge Catholics around the world.

entities.summary: Monsignor François Ducaud-Bourget (1897-1984) was a prominent traditionalist Roman Catholic French prelate, priest, and close ally of Archbishop Marcel Lefebvre. Born in Bordeaux, France, Ducaud-Bourget played a crucial role in shaping the modern traditionalist movement within the Catholic Church. His involvement with the Society of St. Pius X, founded by Lefebvre, helped to establish the movement's headquarters in Rouen, France, and its publication, the journal Nova et Vetera. Ducaud-Bourget's leadership and theological expertise were instrumental in shaping the movement's stance on issues such as the legitimacy of the Second Vatican Council and the use of the Tridentine Mass. Through his tireless advocacy and unwavering commitment to traditionalist principles, Ducaud-Bourget left an indelible mark on the Catholic Church's modern era. His legacy continues to influence the movement's growth and development to this day.
